The supplied coordinating *and* joins two infinitives across an asyndetic Greek seam, and no source token licenses it (rule 5, with 2CO.3.7 and REV.15.6). The verse's two expressed `καί` tokens are both spent, on *and undefiled* and on *and widows*, and neither governs this juncture. Rule 88 is scoped to a participle converted into a coordinate finite clause and does not reach a seam between two infinitives both rendered as infinitives; rule 29's numeral juncture is narrower still. Rule 11 does not decide it either way — the ASV does italicize this *and* — and rule 37 is ruled out, no licensing conjunction standing in a neighbouring verse.

The Greek coordinates the two infinitives asyndetically — no καί stands between `ἐπισκέπτεσθαι` and `τηρεῖν`, the verse's two expressed conjunctions being spent on *and undefiled* and *and widows* — so the supplied *and* is `added` and only *to keep* stands here. Rule 88 does not reach it: that rule is scoped in terms to where the ASV **converts a Greek circumstantial participle into a coordinate finite clause**, and no conversion happens here, both infinitives being rendered as infinitives. 2CO.3.7 is the governing precedent and is the corpus's one test of that limit decided after rule 88 entered the contract: it marks the identical supplied *and* `added` across an asyndetic seam between two attributive participles, citing rule 5 with REV.15.6 and conceding nothing. Rule 86's test gives the same answer — a participle carries subordination, which is why rule 86 grants it a supplied *when* or *if*, but an infinitive carries no coordination, so no token licenses the juncture. TIT.2.9 `εἶναι` → *and to be* is the one contrary unit and is weak evidence: its note cites no rule and it was finished before rule 88 existed. The infinitival *to* is a rule 7 helper on its own verb under rule 61, no conjunction governing the clause. Head on the lexical verb under rule 17.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged: no unit's edges or head were altered. Two notes were tightened only — s002 no longer calls καθαρά a fronted predicate (the ASV simply places the adjective before the noun), and s020 now records its discontinuity from τηρεῖν under rule 15.
Partition checked: all 25 s### and all 28 t### ids appear exactly once, with one unrepresented unit (s017) and no added units.

The verse decides two articles in opposite directions and that is deliberate, not an inconsistency. s006 takes the supplied *our* under rule 20's second arm because no other source word competes for the slot; s017 is `unrepresented` because αὐτῶν stands free to take *their*. Rule 76's availability test is what makes these one analysis rather than two, and the ASV's own markup agrees, italicizing neither.

The supplied *and* at t021 (ASV-marked) is the one genuinely contested call. It is placed as a rule 29/88 juncture helper on τηρεῖν, the verb it introduces; the `added` reading under rule 86 is named and answered in that unit's note. A reference comparison that expects `added` there is not a correction.

Heads reviewed separately from edges under rule 28: each infinitive heads on its lexical verb rather than the infinitival marker (t013, t023), ὀρφανούς heads on the substantival adjective rather than the supplied *the* (t015), and ἄσπιλον heads on its single word *unspotted*.

Variant SBLGNT.JAS.1.27.v011 covers s006, is underdetermined to r00-base, and carries no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark, so rules 12 and 97 leave the projection untouched and nothing here is `added` on textual grounds.
